heading: Series membership / frequency scan without a sample bound
text:
### Series membership / frequency scan without a sample bound [LNLS.3.11]

A `contains(s, v)` or `count_of(s, v)` read over a **series** `s` whose
declaration carries no `capacity` ([LSER.13.14]) is a compile error
(`DS_VALIDATE_NOLINSCAN_SERIES_UNBOUNDED`) in a program with
`linear_scan: false`. The same applies to any series read whose cost is linear in
the window's sample depth.

| Read | Without `capacity` | With `capacity N` |
|---|---|---|
| `contains(cursor, value)` | O(D) window scan | O(N) = O(1) |
| `count_of(cursor, value)` | O(D) window scan | O(N) = O(1) |

**Rationale**: these reads scan the window's stored samples — O(D), where D is
the series depth.  On a `sliding` (or other time-windowed) backing with no
`capacity`, D is O(window × event-rate): it grows with the event trace, is
not a compile-time constant, and the read is a linear scan in series depth
([LNLS.1.1]).  The O(1)-incremental reads — `count`, `sum`, `mean`, `min`,
`max`, `first`, `last`, `bool_and`, `bool_or` — do not scan and are unaffected.

With `capacity N` the scan is O(N), bounded by a compile-time constant —
exactly the discipline `linear_scan: false` applies to bounded strings ([LNLS.3.10]) —
and is allowed.

This is the same cut `realtime` makes from the WCET side ([LNLS.2.3]).
